entities.summary: John Coit Spooner was an American lawyer and Republican politician from Hudson, Wisconsin. He represented Wisconsin as a United States Senator from 1885 to 1891, then again from 1897 to 1907. In his latter stint, he was chairman of the powerful Senate Rules Committee and was considered one of the "Big Four" key Republicans in the Senate who largely controlled its major decisions, the others being Orville H. Platt of Connecticut, William B. Allison of Iowa, and Nelson W. Aldrich of Rhode Island. He is possibly best known for the Spooner Act, which authorized the United States purchase of the Panama Canal Zone.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Spooner Act authorized the United States purchase of the Panama Canal Zone in 1904, significantly impacting global trade and commerce. This acquisition solidified American influence in Central America and marked a major milestone in the country's expansionist policies.
